newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council unconciliatory over television directive.
newsitem.headline: Council unconciliatory over television directive.

text.p: The European Parliament's two key amendments to the television without frontiers directive gained little sympathy with the Culture Council on Monday.
The Council and Parliament are now expected to go to conciliation in 1997 in a bid to settle their differences.

The Parliament demanded in its November 11 vote that the Council's Common Position be amended to demand that all new television sets be equipped with so-called V-Chips to allow parents to screen out violent programmes from their children.
The Council, however, said that while something should be done a V-chip was not necessarily the most efficient way and the issue required further study.
The Parliament had also demanded that the EU insert into the directive -- 89/552/EEC -- the need to guarantee access to major sports events like the soccer world cup on television.
The Council questioned whether the directive was the appropriate place to tackle the problem.
